paper_metadata.title: Microstructure, mechanical properties and oxidation behavior of NbTaTi and NbTaZr refractory alloys

evidence.quote: This study reports the microstructure, phase composition, mechanical properties and oxidation behavior of NbTaTi and NbTaZr ternary equiatomic alloys.
This study reports the microstructure, phase composition, mechanical properties and oxidation behavior of NbTaTi and NbTaZr ternary equiatomic alloys.

samples.material_state: hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) at 1400 °C for 3 h, 210 MPa
hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) at 1400 °C for 3 h, 210 MPa

evidence.quote: The NbTaTi and NbTaZr were prepared by vacuum arc melting from the high purity (≥99.9%) elements. Each alloy was solidified inside a copper cavity, where it was prepared, and had a flattened cigar shape.

After solidification, the alloy samples were wrapped in a Ta foil and hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) under a hydrostatic pressure of a high purity argon of 210 MPa at 1400 °C for 3 h. Heating and cooling rates were 15 °C/min.

The NbTaTi and NbTaZr were prepared by vacuum arc melting from the high purity (≥99.9%) elements. Each alloy was solidified inside a copper cavity, where it was prepared, and had a flattened cigar shape.

After solidification, the alloy samples were wrapped in a Ta foil and hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) under a hydrostatic pressure of a high purity argon of 210 MPa at 1400 °C for 3 h. Heating and cooling rates were 15 °C/min.

evidence.quote: the nano-lamellae, which looked brighter on the BSE images, were rich in Nb and Ta

evidence.quote: the nano-lamellae, which looked dark on the BSE images, were rich with Zr and depleted in Nb and Ta

phases_and_microstructures.name: HCP
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) at 1400 °C for 3 h, 210 MPa

evidence.quote: It is quite possible that these coarse particles were present during HIP at 1400 °C, together with the matrix phase, thus preventing the matrix grains to grow and explaining the relatively low grain size in this alloy. The volume fraction of the coarse, Zr-rich particles was estimated to be ~5–8%.

phases_and_microstructures.name: coarse polygonal grains
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) at 1400 °C for 3 h, 210 MPa

evidence.quote: The microstructure of NbTaTi after HIP consisted of coarse, polygonal grains of ~0.4 mm in diameter (Fig. 4a).

phases_and_microstructures.name: Ti-rich precipitates
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) at 1400 °C for 3 h, 210 MPa

attributes.location: inside grains and at grain boundaries

evidence.quote: Higher magnification images revealed precipitation of secondary phases, both inside grains and at grain boundaries (Fig. 4b).

phases_and_microstructures.name: coarse equiaxed grains
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) at 1400 °C for 3 h, 210 MPa

evidence.quote: The microstructure of NbTaZr was very different from that of NbTaTi. It consisted of finer equiaxed grains of ~40 µm in diameter (Fig. 6a).

phases_and_microstructures.name: nano-lamellar mixture
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) at 1400 °C for 3 h, 210 MPa

evidence.quote: The grain interior consisted of the nano-lamellar mixture of two co-continuous phases (Fig. 6b, c).

phases_and_microstructures.name: coarse Zr-rich particles
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) at 1400 °C for 3 h, 210 MPa

evidence.quote: Coarse, needle-like or plate-like, dark second-phase particles were present at grain boundaries, some of which propagated inside the grains.

mechanisms.name: spinodal decomposition
mechanisms.material_state: hot isostatic pressed (HIP'd) at 1400 °C for 3 h, 210 MPa

evidence.quote: CALPHAD calculations for NbTaZr indicate that the alloy solidifies in the temperature range of 2250–1906 °C to a high-temperature BCC phase, which experiences spinodal decomposition in two BCC phases at T ≤ 1319 °C, one of which (BCC1) is rich in Nb and Ta and another (BCC2) is rich in Zr (Fig. 13b).
